paper_metadata.title: Design and Implementation of a Quantum Computing-Based Financial Portfolio Optimization System

summary: The paper proposes using QAOA for portfolio optimization but only reports a MATLAB simulation producing optimal weights for a 4‑asset portfolio (0.3774, 0.1302, 0.0824, 0.41) with an expected portfolio return of 0.09. No quantum hardware, simulator execution, qubit counts, or circuit metrics are provided.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum portfolio optimization using a QAOA-style hybrid quantum-classical circuit, implemented in MATLAB and evaluated on historical financial data with reported optimal portfolio weights and expected return.

algorithm.ansatz: parameterized QAOA ansatz with alternating single-qubit rotation and entangling layers
algorithm.optimizer: classical optimization algorithm (not specified; examples mentioned: gradient descent, Nelder-Mead)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: portfolio optimization encoded into a quantum circuit with qubits representing assets and objective/constraint terms mapped into the QAOA cost Hamiltonian; exact binary-variable count not reported
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize portfolio return while minimizing risk, subject to budget and diversification constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: encoded via QAOA cost function / penalty-style objective terms; exact method not specified

problem_instance.description: financial portfolio optimization over assets with historical market data; simulation output reports optimal weights for a 4-asset portfolio
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: uses historical financial data; mentions data preprocessing and risk analysis, but exact preprocessing steps are not specified
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compared against conventional optimization methods; simulation results reported optimal portfolio weights and expected portfolio return
